3	import (
4		"reflect"
5		"strings"
6		"testing"
7	)
8	
9	// Regression for reusing a freed name as an independent registration after a
10	// rename, then pointing the renamed dataset at it. raw feeds mid; mid feeds
11	// detail; detail feeds report; raw also feeds the unrelated side. Renaming mid
12	// to hub frees the name mid, which is then registered as a new source with no
13	// upstreams and given its own downstream midchild first. Re-registering hub
14	// with mid as its only direct upstream must succeed: mid and hub are two
15	// independent registrations, hub keeps its original downstream chain, raw
16	// drops hub from its children but keeps side, and hub lands at the end of
17	// mid's child list behind midchild. Afterwards raw's impact scope is just
18	// side, while mid reaches hub, detail and report at distances 1, 2 and 3, and
19	// report's provenance runs detail <- hub <- mid with raw gone.
20	func TestRenameThenReuseFreedNameAsUpstream(t *testing.T) {
21		graph := buildRegisteredGraph(t, [][]string{
22			{"raw"},
23			{"mid", "raw"},
24			{"detail", "mid"},
25			{"report", "detail"},
26			{"side", "raw"}, // unrelated downstream of raw
27		})
28		assertConsistent(t, graph)
29	
30		// Rename the middle dataset: the name mid is freed, the node keeps its
31		// exact position, and every neighbor reference is rewired in place.
32		mustRename(t, graph, "mid", "hub")
33		assertConsistent(t, graph)
34		assertEntry(t, graph, "raw", nil, []string{"hub", "side"})
35		assertEntry(t, graph, "hub", []string{"raw"}, []string{"detail"})
36		assertEntry(t, graph, "detail", []string{"hub"}, []string{"report"})
37		assertEntry(t, graph, "report", []string{"detail"}, nil)
38		assertEntry(t, graph, "side", []string{"raw"}, nil)
39	
40		// While mid is still unregistered it cannot be hub's upstream: the error
41		// names mid, and the rejection is atomic.
42		beforeRejected := snapshot(graph)
43		rawImpactsBeforeRejected := mustImpacts(t, graph, "raw")
44		err := Register(graph, Dataset{Name: "hub"}, []string{"mid"})
45		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown parent") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "mid") {
46			t.Fatalf("want unknown-parent error naming mid, got %v", err)
47		}
48		if !reflect.DeepEqual(snapshot(graph), beforeRejected) {
49			t.Fatalf("rejected registration changed graph: before=%v after=%v", beforeRejected, snapshot(graph))
50		}
51		assertEntry(t, graph, "hub", []string{"raw"}, []string{"detail"})
52		assertEntry(t, graph, "raw", nil, []string{"hub", "side"})
53		if got := mustImpacts(t, graph, "raw"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, rawImpactsBeforeRejected) {
54			t.Fatalf("impacts after rejected registration = %v, want %v", got, rawImpactsBeforeRejected)
55		}
56		assertConsistent(t, graph)
57	
58		// Register mid as a brand-new source with no upstreams, and let it own
59		// another downstream first. It is an independent registration, unrelated
60		// to the renamed hub.
61		mustRegister(t, graph, "mid")
62		mustRegister(t, graph, "midchild", "mid")
63		assertConsistent(t, graph)
64		assertEntry(t, graph, "mid", nil, []string{"midchild"})
65		assertEntry(t, graph, "midchild", []string{"mid"}, nil)
66	
67		// Mixing the legitimate new source with hub's own downstream report must
68		// be refused as a whole: report reaches hub through detail, so the edge
69		// hub -> report would close a cycle. The error names report and the cycle,
70		// and the valid mid listed first must not have changed anything.
71		beforeCycle := snapshot(graph)
72		rawImpactsBeforeCycle := mustImpacts(t, graph, "raw")
73		reportUpstreamsBeforeCycle := mustUpstreams(t, graph, "report")
74		err = Register(graph, Dataset{Name: "hub"}, []string{"mid", "report"})
75		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "cycle") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "report") {
76			t.Fatalf("want cycle error naming report, got %v", err)
77		}
78		if !reflect.DeepEqual(snapshot(graph), beforeCycle) {
79			t.Fatalf("rejected cyclic registration changed graph: before=%v after=%v", beforeCycle, snapshot(graph))
80		}
81		assertEntry(t, graph, "hub", []string{"raw"}, []string{"detail"})
82		assertEntry(t, graph, "mid", nil, []string{"midchild"})
83		assertEntry(t, graph, "raw", nil, []string{"hub", "side"})
84		if got := mustImpacts(t, graph, "raw"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, rawImpactsBeforeCycle) {
85			t.Fatalf("impacts after rejected cyclic registration = %v, want %v", got, rawImpactsBeforeCycle)
86		}
87		if got := mustUpstreams(t, graph, "report"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, reportUpstreamsBeforeCycle) {
88			t.Fatalf("report upstreams after rejected cyclic registration = %v, want %v", got, reportUpstreamsBeforeCycle)
89		}
90		assertConsistent(t, graph)
91	
92		// Replace hub's direct upstreams wholesale with the reused name mid. This
93		// must succeed: mid and hub are independent registrations, and the edge
94		// mid -> hub closes no cycle.
95		mustRegister(t, graph, "hub", "mid")
96		assertConsistent(t, graph)
97	
98		// The graph now holds two independent registrations under the old and new
99		// names. raw released hub but keeps its unrelated downstream side; mid
100		// keeps its own downstream midchild and gains hub appended at the end;
101		// hub keeps its original downstream chain untouched.
102		if got, want := len(graph), 7; got != want {
103			t.Fatalf("dataset count = %d, want %d", got, want)
104		}
105		assertEntry(t, graph, "raw", nil, []string{"side"})
106		assertEntry(t, graph, "mid", nil, []string{"midchild", "hub"})
107		assertEntry(t, graph, "hub", []string{"mid"}, []string{"detail"})
108		assertEntry(t, graph, "detail", []string{"hub"}, []string{"report"})
109		assertEntry(t, graph, "report", []string{"detail"}, nil)
110		assertEntry(t, graph, "midchild", []string{"mid"}, nil)
111		assertEntry(t, graph, "side", []string{"raw"}, nil)
112	
113		// From raw the whole moved chain is gone; only the unrelated side remains.
114		wantRawImpacts := []Impact{
115			{Dataset: "side", Distance: 1, Path: []string{"raw", "side"}},
116		}
117		rawImpacts := mustImpacts(t, graph, "raw")
118		if !reflect.DeepEqual(rawImpacts, wantRawImpacts) {
119			t.Fatalf("impacts from raw = %v, want %v", rawImpacts, wantRawImpacts)
120		}
121	
122		// From mid the chain unfolds along mid -> hub -> detail -> report at
123		// distances 1, 2 and 3, with midchild as mid's other direct downstream.
124		wantMidImpacts := []Impact{
125			{Dataset: "hub", Distance: 1, Path: []string{"mid", "hub"}},
126			{Dataset: "midchild", Distance: 1, Path: []string{"mid", "midchild"}},
127			{Dataset: "detail", Distance: 2, Path: []string{"mid", "hub", "detail"}},
128			{Dataset: "report", Distance: 3, Path: []string{"mid", "hub", "detail", "report"}},
129		}
130		midImpacts := mustImpacts(t, graph, "mid")
131		if !reflect.DeepEqual(midImpacts, wantMidImpacts) {
132			t.Fatalf("impacts from mid = %v, want %v", midImpacts, wantMidImpacts)
133		}
134		assertImpactOnce(t, midImpacts, "hub", 1, []string{"mid", "hub"})
135		assertImpactOnce(t, midImpacts, "detail", 2, []string{"mid", "hub", "detail"})
136		assertImpactOnce(t, midImpacts, "report", 3, []string{"mid", "hub", "detail", "report"})
137	
138		// Tracing report's provenance walks detail, hub, mid in order; raw is no
139		// longer a source of report. Paths are written along the actual
140		// derivation direction, from each source toward report.
141		wantReportUpstreams := []Upstream{
142			{Dataset: "detail", Distance: 1, Path: []string{"detail", "report"}},
143			{Dataset: "hub", Distance: 2, Path: []string{"hub", "detail", "report"}},
144			{Dataset: "mid", Distance: 3, Path: []string{"mid", "hub", "detail", "report"}},
145		}
146		reportUpstreams := mustUpstreams(t, graph, "report")
147		if !reflect.DeepEqual(reportUpstreams, wantReportUpstreams) {
148			t.Fatalf("upstreams of report = %v, want %v", reportUpstreams, wantReportUpstreams)
149		}
150		assertUpstreamOnce(t, reportUpstreams, "mid", 3, []string{"mid", "hub", "detail", "report"})
151		for _, up := range reportUpstreams {
152			if up.Dataset == "raw" {
153				t.Fatalf("raw leaked into report upstreams after replacement: %v", reportUpstreams)
154			}
155		}
156	}

10	// The cutoff regressions here pin down that a cutoff list acts on the names
11	// registered at query time, after a cutoff dataset has been renamed and its old
12	// name has then been registered again for a brand-new dataset.
13	//
14	// The lineage starts as a single chain:
15	//
16	//	source -> cut -> report -> view
17	//
18	// cut is then renamed to gate; the renamed node keeps cut's exact dependency
19	// position (source -> gate -> report -> view), and the old name cut is
20	// unregistered. Only afterwards is cut registered again as a brand-new dataset
21	// under source and given its own downstream bridge, and report is made to
22	// depend on both gate and bridge. The final lineage is:
23	//
24	//	source -> gate ---> report -> view
25	//	  |                  ^
26	//	  +-> cut -> bridge -+
27	//
28	// gate is the renamed original node (its old dependency position, including
29	// its direct downstream report, moved with it); cut is a fresh registration
30	// whose only downstream is bridge. The two identities must never be confused:
31	// a cutoff named cut stops the new cut subtree, not the gate subtree, and
32	// propagation into report over the gate branch must not stop merely because the
33	// gate node used to carry the name cut.
34	
35	// buildRenamedCutoffThenReuseGraph builds the initial source -> cut -> report
36	// -> view chain, renames cut to gate keeping its dependency position, then
37	// registers cut afresh under source with its own downstream bridge and makes
38	// report depend on both gate and bridge. It stops at the requested phase so the
39	// unregistered-old-name window (after the rename, before the re-registration)
40	// can be tested on its own.
41	func buildRenamedCutoffThenReuseGraph(t *testing.T, phase string) map[string]*Lineage {
42		t.Helper()
43		graph := buildRegisteredGraph(t, [][]string{
44			{"source"},
45			{"cut", "source"},
46			{"report", "cut"},
47			{"view", "report"},
48		})
49		assertConsistent(t, graph)
50	
51		mustRename(t, graph, "cut", "gate")
52		assertConsistent(t, graph)
53		// The rename keeps the original dependency position: gate is now the node
54		// between source and report, and the old name is gone from the registry.
55		assertEntry(t, graph, "gate", []string{"source"}, []string{"report"})
56		assertEntry(t, graph, "source", nil, []string{"gate"})
57		assertEntry(t, graph, "report", []string{"gate"}, []string{"view"})
58		assertEntry(t, graph, "view", []string{"report"}, nil)
59		if _, ok := graph["cut"]; ok {
60			t.Fatalf("old name cut still registered after rename")
61		}
62	
63		if phase == "renamed" {
64			return graph
65		}
66		if phase != "reregistered" {
67			t.Fatalf("unknown phase %q", phase)
68		}
69	
70		// Register cut as a brand-new dataset under source, with its own downstream
71		// bridge. It inherits nothing from gate: gate's direct downstream report
72		// must not be copied onto the fresh cut node.
73		mustRegister(t, graph, "cut", "source")
74		mustRegister(t, graph, "bridge", "cut")
75		// report now derives from both the renamed gate and the new bridge; its own
76		// downstream view is retained.
77		mustRegister(t, graph, "report", "gate", "bridge")
78		assertConsistent(t, graph)
79		assertEntry(t, graph, "cut", []string{"source"}, []string{"bridge"})
80		assertEntry(t, graph, "bridge", []string{"cut"}, []string{"report"})
81		assertEntry(t, graph, "gate", []string{"source"}, []string{"report"})
82		assertEntry(t, graph, "source", nil, []string{"gate", "cut"})
83		assertEntry(t, graph, "report", []string{"gate", "bridge"}, []string{"view"})
84		assertEntry(t, graph, "view", []string{"report"}, nil)
85		if got, want := len(graph), 6; got != want {
86			t.Fatalf("dataset count = %d, want %d", got, want)
87		}

89	}

92	// registered cutoff — it stays in the result at distance 1 and stops
